title: Adam and Eve (24 December)
hookLine: some old calendars honor our first parents on Christmas Eve

lines: THE GARDEN NEXT TO THE MANGER.
cards: On the day before Christmas, some old calendars of saints didn't name a martyr or a bishop. They named two people from the very first pages of the Bible: Adam and Eve.
Tradition says that in parts of medieval Europe, people acted out the story of the garden around this day, with a tree hung with fruit standing in the middle of the stage.
Some historians connect that tree, at least in part, with the Christmas tree. So why would anyone put the garden right next to the manger?

teach.h: MUD AND BREATH: A LIVING SOUL.
teach.b: Genesis tells it this way, in the Douay-Rheims: "And the Lord God formed man of the slime of the earth: and breathed into his face the breath of life, and man became a living soul."
Mud and breath: made of the ground, alive with God's own breath. Then the woman, made from Adam's side, and a garden with one tree whose fruit they are told not to eat.
The text never says apple; it says the fruit of the tree. The apple came later, in art and plays. They eat, they hide, they are sent out of the garden.
And before they leave, Adam names his wife.

teach.h: EVE: MOTHER OF ALL THE LIVING.
teach.b: "And Adam called the name of his wife Eve, because she was the mother of all the living." Even at the edge of paradise, the story puts a name of life on her. That's why the day before Christmas fits.
Catholic tradition reads the Bible as one story, and Christmas as a turning point in it.

teach.h: IN ADAM ALL DIE; IN CHRIST, ALIVE.
teach.b: Paul puts the two ends side by side: "And as in Adam all die, so also in Christ all shall be made alive." He even calls Christ the last Adam.
Early Christian writers added a second pair, calling Mary the new Eve, the woman whose yes undoes the first no.
So on Christmas Eve, the old calendars remembered the first parents, waiting, as it were, at the door of the stable. And one more thing in Eve's name.

teach.h: THE MOTHER OF ALL THE LIVING.
teach.b: If she is the mother of all the living, then every person you meet is, in this story, a cousin.

how: Adam and Eve are not on today's General Roman Calendar, but some older Western calendars and devotions remembered them on 24 December, and Catholics hear the garden story at Mass on the feast of the Immaculate Conception, where it is set beside Mary.

games.q: Adam names his wife Eve before they leave the garden. what reason does Genesis give for the name?
o: because she was taken out of man
because she was the mother of all the living
because she ate the fruit first
games.why: mother of all the living. taken out of man is the reason Genesis gives earlier for the word woman.

practice: Notice your breath, the breath of life in the story, and begin with one face, someone close to you; then widen to your street, your town, the people you argue with, strangers across the world, until the circle holds everyone.
If you pray, say the first two words of the Lord's Prayer, Our Father, and notice the word our; if you don't, let the word family stretch as far as it will go.

wordCard.voice: Eve. In Genesis, with Adam, the first parents, made of earth and breath, remembered in some old calendars on Christmas Eve, the night the story turns.

orig.note: Hebrew: Eve's name. Genesis gives the reason right away: she was the mother of all the living.

carryVoice: Your line: the first parents. Made of mud and breath, and given a name of life. I'll be here tomorrow.
